acceptance_criteria: the objectives prompt section states that recorded text is shown to the owner verbatim and must be second person, never 'the owner', never naming the machine
tests/test_objective_prompt.py asserts those rules in the rendered prompt; the rest of the prompt is unchanged
prohibited_actions: deploy, promote to production, restart services or change systemd/launchd/watchers
read, add or change secrets, credentials or tokens
Shopify, Gmail, Stripe or any other business write, or any external send
change reviewer principals, owner authority, permissions or connector/MCP access
destructive repository cleanup or history rewriting
change the frozen engineering lifecycle kernel
requested_outcome: Mobile dogfood (2026-09-23): the objective records CLIVE writes are read by George on his phone, but the Ethiopia objective's blocker read 'No flight booking ... tool on this Mac — those steps need to be done by the owner or son directly', addressing George in the third person and naming a Mac while CLIVE runs on a Linux server. Fix the source: the '# Objectives the owner keeps alive' section of SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE in app/kb/loader.py must tell CLIVE that everything it records on an objective (facts, unknowns, blockers, questions, work items) is shown to the owner verbatim, so it writes to him in the second person ('you', 'your son'), never 'the owner', and never names the machine CLIVE runs on. Add tests/test_objective_prompt.py asserting the rendered system prompt carries these rules. Change nothing else in the prompt.
title: Mobile Alpha dogfood: objective records speak to George
